messages:
maria: Heads-up — after the kernel swap on canary, latency for long sequences spiked ~2.4x. Traces uploaded: s3://redwood-perf/canary/2501234567/*.tgz. Looks like batch formation is favoring short requests and long seqs are starving in mixed-tenant queues. @raj any quick thoughts?

raj: Saw that. Repro steps I used: 
```
./bin/perf_profile --host canary1 --duration 60 --collect=latency,kv
```
Quick hypothesis: new kernel reduces per-token time for tiny sequences, so short jobs complete faster and the batcher (which counts slots, not token-cost) fills with shorts. Long requests keep waiting because token_budget refills are timed to slot granularity rather than token weight.

sasha: Adding telemetry: KV warmup hit% for long sequences dropped from ~78% -> ~52% for tenant A during the canary window. That amplifies long tail.

lee: Context: tenant A short:long request ratio ~12:1. Typical tokens: short ~8 tok, long ~512 tok. With token_budget_target=200 we basically never let a long request grab enough slot budget — they get preempted by many shorts.

maria: Quick mitigation proposal: make batch formation token-weighted. Pseudo patch below: 
```
# cohort slot cost (pseudo)
if cohort_slot_mode == 'weighted':
  slot_cost = max(1, (req.tokens + 63) // 64)
  allocate_slots(slot_cost)
else:
  allocate_slots(1)
```
Expose as runtime flag `--cohort-slot-mode=weighted`. This keeps short jobs cheap but prevents unlimited piling on short slots that starve long ones.

raj: Also consider a small reserved lane for large sequences: reserve N slots per cohort for req.tokens > 256. That avoids full starvation on pathological ratios.

sasha: Telemetry we need before/after: token_distribution_hist, kv_hit_by_length_bucket, queue_wait_seconds_by_length, per-tenant_slot_utilization. I'll add counters and mark them for 30s scrape.

qabot: perf-smoke results on canary2: 10/12 tests passed, 2 flaky (kv warmup timing). No error rate spike.

lee: Can we also try a per-tenant override bump: token_budget_target=800 for tenant A to see immediate effect while we iterate on the allocator?

maria: Good idea. I'll run a canary that combines weighted slots + tenant override for A. Plan: deploy to canary cluster, run 30m synthetic replay, gather kv-hit and wait-time. Will post results in ~30m. Any objections to short rollout?

raj: No objections. Add an automatic rollback if error_rate > 1% or p95 latency for short seqs increases > 10%.

sasha: One more thought: kernel selection currently picks the low-latency fast-path for small sequences. We may want a kernel affinity hint so long sequences use a kernel variant optimized for KV locality and steady throughput. A header like `X-Kernel-Hint: kv-local` could do this on canary.

maria: Good call, i'll add `X-Kernel-Hint: kv-local` for long seqs in the canary. Also enabling cohort-slot-mode=weighted on canary.

ops-bot: deploy-bot started canary deploy for cohort-slot-mode=weighted on canary-cluster. Tracing enabled.

maria: Quick canary update: after 25m run — short tail latency unchanged, median long latency down ~30%, kv-hit up from 52% -> 68% for tenant A, queue wait for long reqs down ~60%. Early signal looks good. Next steps: run 12h replay, add rollback scripts, and draft rollout notes (A/B ramp + per-tenant overrides). Thanks all! :party_parrot:
